annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee: Interdependences between AI applications and liberal professions services: addressing urgent societal needs
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee: Interdependences between AI applications and liberal professions services: addressing urgent societal needs
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C series
annotation.summary_en: European Economic and Social Committee opinion on AI use in the liberal professions (doctors, lawyers, engineers, accountants). It insists on 'human in command', explainability, clear liability rules, GDPR compliance, training and professional self-regulation, and urges a renewed AI Liability Directive. It has no robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: 'Human in command' must always be guaranteed; AI complements rather than replaces liberal professions.
Introduce a European AI 'quality seal' and regulatory sandboxes for AI in the liberal professions.
Professionals bear primary responsibility, but developers keep their own liability; a new AI Liability Directive attempt is urged.
Professional chambers should update codes of conduct and provide AI training; expand AI training via Erasmus+ and ESF.
Strengthen European computing infrastructure and digital sovereignty; involve liberal professions in AI regulation.
